title: Melting and freezing
card: Warm ice on the burner, then cool it.

predict.prompt: You warm a block of ice from the freezer on the burner. At what temperature will it melt?

try: Tap WARM to heat the beaker on the burner. Tap COOL to stand it in an ice bath. Watch the thermometer!
safety: In a real lab, only a grown-up lights the burner. Never play with fire at home.
result: The ice melted into water at 0 °C, and the water boiled into steam at 100 °C. Cooled in the ice bath, the water froze into ice again at 0 °C.
why: Ice, water and steam are all water: a solid, a liquid and a gas. Warming water or cooling it changes its state.
Ice melts at 0 °C and water boils at 100 °C (at sea level). While the ice melts or the water boils, the thermometer stays still: the heat goes into changing the state.
Cooling works the other way round: steam turns back into water, and water freezes into ice at 0 °C. The ice bath is ice with salt, which gets colder than 0 °C.
